payload.title: Executor pool for codex-cli/codex-readonly/codex-pi/codex-herdr/codex-bwrap all hardcode…
payload.description: Executor pool for codex-cli/codex-readonly/codex-pi/codex-herdr/codex-bwrap all hardcode CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn (confirmed in .fgos/config.json), so every concurrent session's codex dispatch shares one account's quota regardless of the codex-tetnu/codex-tetcu72 accounts that exist as shell aliases. Similarly claude/claude-reviewer executors have zero account-isolation env var (unlike codex's CODEX_HOME), so every concurrent session's claude dispatch shares one default account's session limit. Confirmed live 2026-09-15/16: real quota/session-limit walls hit twice each during code-panel-multicell-facade track execution, forcing executor swaps and dispatch retries. Fix direction: register account-rotating executor variants (or round-robin within one executor entry) for both codex and claude pools so concurrent multi-session dispatch load doesn't concentrate on one account.
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.title: dispatch recover's resume-driver action (and likely other action types) bumps the target Run's…
payload.description: dispatch recover's resume-driver action (and likely other action types) bumps the target Run's controlEpoch and writes a recovery-commands.jsonl entry, but does NOT clear the separate per-assignment dispatch.claim lockfile (.fgos/assignments/<id>/dispatch.claim) that createAndExecuteSessionTask checks before permitting a new dispatch attempt for that assignment. Confirmed live 2026-09-16: a coordination-session-owned Run whose wrapping process was killed (system memory pressure) left status:running with a stale dispatch.claim; calling dispatch recover with a fresh recommendation and applying it (outcome:applied, controlEpoch bumped) did NOT unblock a retry -- 'a dispatch is already in progress ... refusing to spawn a second concurrent executor run' still fired until the dispatch.claim file was deleted by hand. Fix direction: the recovery door's own liveness-verified apply path should also remove/invalidate the stale dispatch.claim for the same assignment+run when the action confirms the prior attempt is dead, so recover is a genuinely complete unblock rather than a partial one requiring undocumented manual filesystem cleanup.
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.title: Sharper root cause for tsk-12j: the account-concentration is caused by…
payload.description: Sharper root cause for tsk-12j: the account-concentration is caused by src/runner/dispatch/assignment-runner.mjs:1104-1109's deliberate read-only-assignment executor redirect (resolvedExecutorId = isReadOnlyAssignment(...) && defaultExecutorId==='claude' && cfg.executors['claude-reviewer'] ? 'claude-reviewer' : defaultExecutorId). This is intentional safety (prevent a review/red-team role from getting git-write Bash grants), added per a prior red-team finding (Cell 6.3 Fix Round 1/2) -- but it forces EVERY read-only assignment (review-candidate AND red-team-candidate both declare result.kind:advisory, both classify read-only) onto the SAME 'claude-reviewer' executor regardless of what actors[].executor the request declares, and claude-reviewer itself has zero account isolation (same gap as tsk-12j's original claude/codex finding). Confirmed empirically: 19/19 claude-family dispatches in the code-panel-multicell-facade track resolved to claude-reviewer, including ones explicitly requesting a plain 'claude' executor for the red-team role specifically to diversify load. Fix direction: keep the safety redirect (it is correct and should not be removed) but make it redirect to one of SEVERAL claude-reviewer-family entries (account-isolated variants, mirroring whatever fix tsk-12j lands for the base pool) instead of a single hardcoded 'claude-reviewer' target.
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung
